issues.display_title: Issue #1746: Tour publish fails — permission denied reading moderation image files on server
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Follow-up to #1745 — tour publish stuck for moderation_id=3574652, no row added to Audit table.

Debug Result

Traced via HelperClass.php line 538 (getImageWidth()):

getimagesize(/data/moderation/14290/307371291597519300/20260806001040.b6d59a5272fd.jpg): Failed to open stream: Permission denied

file_exists() succeeds (file present on disk) but getimagesize() fails to open the stream — indicates a file/directory permission issue on the server, not application logic. This blocks the publish flow before the Audit table insert is reached, so the tour never publishes.

Root Cause

Server-side permission issue on /data/moderation/14290/307371291597519300/ (or the file itself) — not a code defect. But now it's already fixed.

Reference

  • Issue: #1745

issues.display_title: Issue #1747: Stop generating invoice for subscription downgrade (Stripe, test users only)
issues.main_description_html:
Background

Currently, when a user downgrades their subscription plan, the system still creates a purchase record and generates an invoice for that downgrade — even though no payment is actually charged at that moment.

Going forward, invoice for downgrade will not be generated at the moment the user downgrades anymore. Instead, it will be generated later by a cronjob (to be built in a follow-up task).

Goal

Downgrade action should no longer generate a purchase record or invoice. A downgrade is a plan change, not a payment event, so it shouldn't produce an invoice.

Scope for this task

  • Applies to Stripe downgrade only.
  • Enabled for test users only (not rolled out to all users yet).

Acceptance Criteria

  • When a test user downgrades via Stripe, no purchase record or invoice is created.
  • Downgrade still completes successfully (plan change, scheduling, and success/failure emails continue to work as before).
  • Non-test users and PayPal downgrades are unaffected by this change.

Result

DowngradeHelper::insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade() gained a $deferInvoice param. When true, the method skips the cc_purchase insert and invoice generation and returns empty link/filename, but CCLog is still written as before. Stripe\Subscription\Downgrade now passes deferInvoice: $this->isTestMode (the existing test-mode flag already computed via HelperClass::isUseStripeTestMode() earlier in handle()), so the skip only applies to Stripe test users. Plan change, scheduling, and success/failure emails are untouched. A follow-up cronjob will need to create both the cc_purchase row and the invoice for these deferred downgrades, since neither exists yet at this point — noted in the method's docblock and inline comment.

Commits: c94e999, 53d097f, 4b87d98 (merged via PR #1748).

issues.display_title: Issue #1749: Stop generating invoice for subscription downgrade (PayPal, test users only)
issues.main_description_html:
Background

Follow-up to #1747, which stopped Stripe subscription downgrades from generating a purchase record and invoice for test users. Invoice for these downgrades will be generated later by a cronjob (separate task).

PayPal downgrade still creates a purchase record and invoice immediately, same as Stripe did before #1747.

Goal

Apply the same behavior to PayPal: downgrade should no longer generate a purchase record or invoice for test users.

Scope for this task

  • Applies to PayPal downgrade only.
  • Enabled for test users only (not rolled out to all users yet).

Acceptance Criteria

  • When a test user downgrades via PayPal, no purchase record or invoice is created.
  • Downgrade still completes successfully (plan change and success/failure emails continue to work as before).
  • Non-test users are unaffected by this change.

Result

PayPal\Subscription\Subscription\Capture\Actions\DowngradeHandler now passes deferInvoice: $this->isTestMode to DowngradeHelper::insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade(), reusing the $deferInvoice param added for Stripe in #1747/#1748 and the $this->isTestMode gate already computed in DowngradeHandler::handle(). No changes needed in the shared helper itself — same skip logic (no cc_purchase insert, no invoice, CCLog still written) now applies to both processors for test users. Plan change and success/failure emails are unaffected.

Commit: 447fee8.

issues.display_title: Issue #1751: Add invoice_id column to cc_purchase table
issues.main_description_html:
Add an invoice_id column to the cc_purchase table (cc_db).

Why

Invoice lookup currently matches purchase records by transid with string variations (see InvoiceHelper::findPurchaseByTransaction / DatabaseClass::tablePurchase()), which is fragile. A dedicated invoice_id column would allow direct, reliable lookup.

Scope

  • Add invoice_id column to cc_purchase (cc_db)
  • Populate/set invoice_id on purchase creation where applicable
  • Update lookup logic to use invoice_id where relevant

issues.display_title: Issue #1752: Remove legacy SubscriptionClass dependency from Stripe subs complete-3ds
issues.main_description_html:
Why

POST /v2/payment/subscription/complete-3ds (Stripe subs 3DS completion) is the only remaining live caller of legacy SubscriptionClass::completeSubs3DS() (app/Class/Payment/SubscriptionClass.php:506). The /subs step itself (Subscription.php) already uses the modern action-class pattern — this is the one piece of the subs flow still routed through the legacy class.

Problem found during review

  • completeSubs3DS() rebuilds a bare (object)['id' => $subsId] stub from the Redis-stashed data and writes users / user_extra_data / cc_purchase as a successful payment unconditionally — there is no status === 'paid' check anywhere in this path.
  • Compare the sibling flow CompleteUpgrade3DS.php:98-102, which retrieves the live subscription + invoice from Stripe and throws unless status === 'paid'. Subs' 3DS-complete has no equivalent guard.
  • FE (useSubscribe.jsx) does gate on paymentIntent.status === 'succeeded' before calling this endpoint, but the backend has no independent verification of its own. A direct call to /complete-3ds with a valid-but-unconfirmed client_secret returned by step 1 would activate the subscription and write a success purchase record without payment ever completing.
  • The one Stripe call that does exist in this path (resolveStripeSubscriptionBillingInterval()) only fetches a billing-interval label for logging, and its catch (ApiErrorException) swallows failures and returns null — completion proceeds regardless, so it can't double as the verification step.

Scope

  • Replace the SubscriptionClass::completeSubs3DS() call in CompleteSubs3DS.php with a modern implementation, following the CompleteUpgrade3DS.php pattern:
    • Retrieve the live subscription + latest_invoice from Stripe
    • Verify the invoice is actually paid before writing anything
    • Move the finalize logic (user/plan update, cc_logs + cc_purchase insert, invoice, email) into the action class or a helper, matching how upgrade does it
  • Remove SubscriptionClass::completeSubs3DS() (and any private helper it alone used) once nothing calls it

Out of scope (separate work)

  • ch_ / invoice_id population on cc_purchase — column tracked in #1751, extraction logic is a follow-up once this endpoint has a real invoice object to read from
  • /subs sync path, /upgrade, /downgrade, /space-addon — not touched here
  • The other dead new SubscriptionClass() instantiations in GetSubStatus.php, CalculateProration.php, SubscriptionController.php (constructed, never called) — cleanup, not correctness, can be its own small PR

Acceptance

  • /complete-3ds rejects finalization when Stripe reports the invoice isn't paid (mirrors upgrade's behavior)
  • No code path calls SubscriptionClass::completeSubs3DS() anymore
  • Existing 3DS subscribe flow still completes end-to-end against a Stripe test-mode 3DS card
